finding.observed: The monotonicity proof treats the same derivation as valid after enlarging its premise set, and the transitivity proof concatenates derivations into an enlarged premise context without rechecking quantifier-rule freshness.
finding.defect: A quantifier-rule eigenvariable absent from the original premise set may occur in added premises. The unchanged sequence can therefore cease to satisfy the rule's side condition; direct concatenation has the same problem.
controlling_evidence: OLP-0115 requires the quantifier-rule parameter to be absent from the entire premise set and the rule's fixed companion formula.

A two-line empty-context derivation from the falsehood axiom to a universally quantified conditional is valid with eigenvariable a, but the same annotated sequence is invalid from a premise set containing R(a).
Every derivation is finite, so only finitely many auxiliary constants are needed to freshen its quantifier-rule applications.
A temporary conservative language extension supplies auxiliary constants outside arbitrary premise sets while leaving all original-language premises and endpoints unchanged.

bounded_repair.monotonicity: Prove premise extension by induction on derivation length; in a quantifier-rule case, uniformly rename a clashing eigenvariable in the shorter premise derivation to a fresh auxiliary constant before applying the induction hypothesis and the rule.
bounded_repair.transitivity: Use repaired monotonicity for the first derivation and uniformly freshen every quantifier-rule eigenvariable of the second derivation that occurs in the added Gamma context before concatenation.
bounded_repair.scope: Preserve both theorem statements, the frozen English source, OLPL-025, OLPL-026 and all unaffected language choices.

routing.upstream: Retain for one deduplicated end-of-translation report; do not open an individual issue.
routing.human_review: Advisory and not a production or publication prerequisite.
